properties.title: Generative Medical Event Models Improve with Scale

membership.reason: Implements Curiosity (S/M/L), an autoregressive medical-event transformer that simulates probabilistic multi-step future patient timelines over chronological clinical events and time-passage tokens.

properties.backbone: Qwen2 decoder-only transformer trained from scratch (1B params, 1.7T training tokens)

properties.flow: Tokenized Epic Cosmos patient history -> Curiosity autoregressive rollout (n=25 1-year simulations) -> Event probability, time-to-event, and utilization forecasts

properties.purpose: Zero-shot simulation-based prediction across 78 clinical diagnosis, prognosis, and healthcare operations tasks.
properties.environment: Retrospective de-identified Epic Cosmos EHR (118M patients)

evidence_fragments.content: Using Epic Cosmos, a dataset with medical events from de-identified longitudinal health records for 16.3 billion encounters over 300 million unique patient records from 310 health systems, we introduce the Curiosity models, a family of decoder-only transformer models pretrained on 118 million patients representing 115 billion discrete medical events (151 billion tokens).

We trained Curiosity using the Qwen2 transformer architecture [18] with random initialization—i.e., without loading any pretrained Qwen2 weights (see Section 5.3 for training details). Three model sizes were trained, as detailed in Table 1.

[paraphrase (visual p.4)] Figure 1 shows the 4-stage Curiosity pipeline: (1) Tokenize Patient chronological health history with time-passage tokens; (2) Prompt Curiosity; (3) Simulate Future via n autoregressive Monte Carlo simulations; (4) Glean Insights (today's visit predictions, differential diagnosis, and 1y/3y disease and utilization risks).

[paraphrase (visual p.5)] Figure 2 compares Curiosity-S, Curiosity-M, and Curiosity-L against best task-specific supervised baselines across Plausibility (Encounter Generation), Disease Risk (Hyperlipidemia Outcomes, Incident Disease, Hypertension Outcomes, Type 2 Diabetes Outcomes, Acute-On-Chronic), Differential Diagnosis, and Patients' Interactions with the Health System (30 Day Readmission, Encounter Forecasting, Length of Stay), showing monotonic improvement with scale.

In Figure 3, calibration curves for Curiosity-L show good calibration for predicting personalized healthcare needs. Across encounter types and counts, the expected calibration error (ECE) [19] improved with model scale (Appendix B).
Conditioned on a patient’s real-world history, Curiosity autoregressively predicts the next medical event to simulate patient health timelines.

Curiosity probabilistically generates n simulations, which are then used to compute all predictions, including event probabilities, distributions, times-to-event, and outcome collections (see Section 5.5 for more details).
We first examined aggregate summary statistics over Curiosity generations, prompting Curiosity to produce 25 1-year generations for 20,000 patients.

capability_assessments.rationale: Autoregressive medical-event transformer (62M-1B) simulating stochastic 1-year and 3-year patient timelines across 78 downstream tasks without settable external action conditioning.

limitations: Trained and evaluated on proprietary Epic Cosmos data (access restricted to contributing health systems).
No settable action interface or causal intervention evaluation.

legacy_cells.B: Generative Medical Event Models Improve with Scale
legacy_cells.C: Waxler, Shane, Blazek, Paul, White, Davis, Sneider, Daniel, Chung, Kevin, Nagarathnam, Mani, et al.
legacy_cells.O: Congestive heart failure, asthma, sickle cell disease, alcohol use disorder, and COPD
legacy_cells.S: Given a patient's longitudinal EHR history, what medical events and outcomes are likely over future time intervals?
legacy_cells.X: F2 EHR / ICU event & latent patient dynamics
legacy_cells.AI: Structured EHR event tokens: demographics; encounters; diagnoses; chief complaints; laboratory results; medication orders; procedures; time
legacy_cells.BL: Elapsed time is tokenized in intervals from 1–5 minutes to 3–6 months; gaps over 6 months use repeated 6-month tokens rounded to the nearest integer.
legacy_cells.BS: Autoregressively generated future medical-event tokens, including diagnoses, medications, lab results, procedures, and encounters
legacy_cells.BX: Pretrained on 118 million patient records, 115 billion medical events, and 151 billion tokens
legacy_cells.CD: Up to 3 years for disease-specific outcome prediction
legacy_cells.CG: 60 sampled trajectories per patient for incident-disease tasks
legacy_cells.DQ: 118 million unique patient records, 115 billion medical events, and 151 billion tokens
legacy_cells.DZ: Event-prevalence and pairwise co-occurrence RMSLE, plus expected calibration error for encounter-count probabilities
legacy_cells.EA: Evaluated generated-event syntactic validity, event prevalence and co-occurrence, and encounter-frequency calibration; authors report multi-token events were rarely invalid.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared against task-specific supervised models, including linear/logistic regression, XGBoost, and supervised Transformers; Curiosity-L achieved 0.770 AUCROC for 30-day readmission versus 0.718 for the best supervised model.
legacy_cells.EL: Invalid multi-token generated events were observed, although rare. Authors also report incomplete or erroneous EHR documentation, missing records across health systems, and left-truncation of histories beyond the 8,192-token context window.
legacy_cells.FB: Patient state is a chronological sequence of discrete, typed medical-event tokens, conditioned on the patient's history; model context is limited to 8,192 tokens.
legacy_cells.FL: A Qwen2 decoder-only Transformer consumes a patient's tokenized EHR history as context, autoregressively samples future event-token trajectories, and derives event probabilities, distributions, and time-to-event predictions from those samples; no planner is implemented.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces the Curiosity medical-event models and training pipeline, evaluates zero-shot generations on a broad suite of clinical tasks, and studies scaling laws for medical-event data.
legacy_cells.FN: Curiosity-L achieved 0.770 AUCROC for 30-day readmission versus 0.718 for the best supervised model. The study evaluated 78 real-world tasks, and predictive performance generally improved with model and pretraining scale.
legacy_cells.FO: Authors cite documentation imprecision and errors, care outside Cosmos causing record gaps, discretization of continuous laboratory values and time, an 8,192-token context window that truncates many patient histories, omitted structured and multimodal data types, phenotype-definition limitations, and lack of prospective validation or subgroup-specific performance and calibration evaluation.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work includes adding structured and multimodal event types, decision-effect estimation and counterfactual consistency, time-to-event analysis, fine-tuning, prospective studies, and human-factors and governance research.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors state that prior medical-event models used smaller or narrower datasets and had not systematically tested how model size and compute should scale on large, diverse patient records.
legacy_cells.FR: The results demonstrate retrospective prediction and event-sequence simulation, not intervention effects: medication events appear in the sequence but are not explicit treatment-action inputs to a transition model. No alternative-action counterfactual comparison, planning/control result, prospective validation, or clinical benefit was demonstrated.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M6 Rollout service; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose future-state forecasts through a time-aware dynamics interface and validate error versus horizon; treatment actions need separate evidence before intervention simulation.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pp. 1–52: title/abstract, introduction, Results §§2.1–2.7, Discussion §§3.1–3.3 including limitations and future work, Related Work, Methods §§5.1–5.6.9, dataset statistics, evaluation tables and figures, and appendices A–J. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: Complete 52-page extracted text reviewed. Some extracted figure/table layouts are disrupted, and the readmission AUC differs slightly between the main text/figure (0.717) and Appendix B Table 14 (0.718); the appendix table value is used. Ambiguous table alignments were not used for other numeric claims. Blueprint module/open-problem mapping fields FS and FU were omitted because the referenced module taxonomy was not included in the supplied inputs. Evidence QA: 71/75 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (94.7%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 71 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 4 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.
